entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK declares neither this nor anything else in the multi-image family (its VTDecompressionSession.h ends at CVImageBuffer in the decode callback) and no release this port builds exports it - _VTDecompressionSessionSetMultiImageCallback is absent from the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 armv7 caches - so the port has to export it
entries.effect: noErr, with the callback and its reference value accepted and NOT stored. MEASURED on this host, 2026-10-03, on an ORDINARY single-image H264 session: the host answers 0, so a port that answered an error would refuse a call the release accepts. WHAT DIFFERS FROM THE HOST is named here: the 26.2 header says of an installed callback 'When installed, outputMultiImageCallback will also be used when DecodeFrame operations fail and return a nonzero status', and on the port a FAILING DECODE STILL REACHES THE SESSION'S SINGLE-IMAGE CALLBACK, because the session is the release's and the release's decode output has no multi-image parameter to carry a failure anywhere else. Nothing is stored in a table: an address-keyed process-global table leaks when a session dies and hands a later session at the same address a callback it was never given, and a value nothing reads is not an installation either
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTDecompressionSession.h:388-401 for the declaration and its discussion; the per-band ladder from tools/corpus/dump-cache.lua over ~/.charon/dyld/4.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7 and the 6.1.3 dump; the release's own decode callback shape is the 16.4 SDK's VTDecompressionSession.h:85-92

entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK does not declare it and no release this port builds exports it (_VTDecompressionSessionDecodeFrameWithMultiImageCapableOutputHandler is absent from the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 armv7 caches), so the port has to export it. What decides it is not the missing symbol but the callback's argument: the handler receives a CMTaggedBufferGroupRef, and the release's own decode callback has no parameter that could receive one
entries.effect: kVTParameterErr (-12902), with the caller's block neither retained nor called and infoFlagsOut LEFT ALONE. MEASURED on this host with a REAL H264 sample (a 221-byte avc1 frame at 64x48, encoded here), because a NULL sample buffer makes every variant answer the same -12902 as plain DecodeFrame and measures nothing: 'DecodeFrameWithMultiImageCapableOutputHandler -> -12902 handler calls=0 infoFlags=0x5a5a5a5a' against 'DecodeFrame (the control) -> 0 single-image calls=1 infoFlags=0' on the SAME session and the SAME sample. The refusal is therefore about the variant, not about the session or the sample, and the header sanctions it - 'If the VTDecompressionSessionDecodeFrameWithMultiImageCapableOutputHandler call returns an error, the block will not be called'
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTDecompressionSession.h:444-480 for the declaration; CMTaggedBufferGroup arrived with iOS 14 and no release the port builds has it, which is the measured cause

entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK does not declare it and no release this port builds exports it (_VTCompressionSessionEncodeMultiImageFrame is absent from the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 armv7 caches), so the port has to export it. Its SOURCE is a CMTaggedBufferGroupRef and no release function reads one: the release's own encode entry point takes a CVImageBuffer
entries.effect: noErr, with kVTEncodeInfo_FrameDropped (bit 0 of VTEncodeInfoFlags, so 0x1) written into infoFlagsOut. MEASURED with a real group - CMTagCollectionCreate(NULL, 0) then CMTaggedBufferGroupCreate over one buffer, matches=1 - and a real session: 'EncodeMultiImageFrame(real group) -> 0 encode callbacks=2 infoFlags=0x1', where the host's own output callback fired ONCE with status -12902 and no sample ('encode callback: calls=2 status=-12902 flags=0 sample=(null)'). NOT REPRODUCED: that callback. The session is the release's and the caller's callback is inside it with no public route out; the release's own encode will not make the call on request, which is measured - 'EncodeFrame(NULL image) -> -12902 callbacks=0 infoFlags=0x5a5a5a5a' - so there is no release call whose effect is to call the caller's callback once with -12902. The two things a caller can read, noErr and the dropped frame, are reproduced; the third is not, and a caller waiting on its output callback for this frame will not hear about it

entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK does not declare it and no release this port builds exports it (_VTCompressionSessionEncodeMultiImageFrameWithOutputHandler is absent from the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 armv7 caches), so the port has to export it. Same source as the function above - a CMTaggedBufferGroupRef - and the block adds a promise this port cannot keep
entries.effect: kVTParameterErr (-12902), with the caller's block neither retained nor called. MEASURED on the same real session and the same real group: 'EncodeMultiImageFrameWithOutputHandler(real) -> -12902 encode callbacks=0'. infoFlagsOut is NOT written, and the 0x1 in that probe line is the value the previous call left in the same word - the probe reused one variable across the two calls, which is the shape of index-by-hand error that has bitten this family twice, so it is named rather than quoted as a measurement
